findings.summary: run_task condition changed from [skyvern_v1, openai_cua] to CUA_ENGINES, dropping RunEngine.skyvern_v1 so explicit skyvern-1.0 requests now raise HTTP 400 "Invalid agent engine"
findings.failure_scenario: Existing API client posts /run/tasks with engine="skyvern-1.0" (valid enum value, previously handled by this branch) -> falls through the skyvern_v2 check -> HTTPException 400 raised at line 1592; previously working task runs are rejected

findings.summary: _call_anthropic sends messages containing OpenAI-format image_url screenshot blocks directly to AsyncAnthropic.messages.create, which only accepts Anthropic-format image blocks
findings.failure_scenario: Run a task with engine="anthropic-cua"; first _generate_anthropic_actions call builds messages via llm_messages_builder_with_history producing {"type":"image_url",...} blocks -> anthropic SDK 0.50.0 param validation (or the API) rejects them -> LLMProviderError -> step fails and the anthropic CUA run can never start

findings.summary: _parse_anthropic_computer_args checks for type=="function" and reads tool_call["function"]["arguments"], but Anthropic tool_use blocks have type=="tool_use" and args under "input", so no action is ever parsed
findings.failure_scenario: Anthropic model returns content with {"type":"tool_use","name":"computer","input":{"action":"mouse_move","coordinate":[x,y]}} -> parser returns None for every block -> parse_anthropic_actions returns [] -> agent_step marks the step failed ("No actions to execute") -> anthropic_cua tasks always fail

findings.summary: Condition inverted from 'engine != RunEngine.openai_cua' to 'engine in CUA_ENGINES' inside the non-CUA else-branch, making run_operation(AgentPhase.llm) dead code for skyvern_v1/v2
findings.failure_scenario: Organization registers an async operation with agent_phase=llm; on any skyvern_v1/v2 run, the else-branch executes with engine in {skyvern_v1, skyvern_v2}, so 'engine in CUA_ENGINES' is always False -> the LLM-phase async operation never runs (previously it fired on every LLM call), silently disabling the feature

findings.summary: Tool results are added with content={"result": ...} (a dict), which is not a valid Anthropic tool_result content type (must be a string or content blocks), so the next LLM call with these in history fails
findings.failure_scenario: After the first successful/failed tool execution, current_tool_results are prepended to message_history; the next _generate_anthropic_actions call sends {"type":"tool_result","tool_use_id":...,"content":{"result":...}} -> anthropic SDK validation error or API 400 -> LLMProviderError -> task fails on the second step

findings.summary: _call_anthropic always passes betas= to ANTHROPIC_CLIENT.messages.create, but with ENABLE_BEDROCK_ANTHROPIC=True the client is AsyncAnthropicBedrock whose create has no betas parameter, and the model name "claude-3-5-sonnet-latest" is not a valid Bedrock model id
findings.failure_scenario: Set ENABLE_BEDROCK_ANTHROPIC=True and run an anthropic-cua task -> AsyncAnthropicBedrock.messages.create raises TypeError (unexpected keyword argument 'betas'), and even without that the stripped model name 'claude-3-5-sonnet-latest' would be rejected by Bedrock -> the Bedrock mode added by this diff is non-functional

findings.summary: LLMCallerManager keeps every per-task LLMCaller (including its full message_history with all base64 screenshots) in a class-level dict forever; clear_llm_caller exists but is never called
findings.failure_scenario: Long-running server executes many anthropic-cua tasks; each LLMCaller's message_history accumulates every step's base64 screenshot (call() assigns self.message_history = messages which embeds screenshots) and is never released -> unbounded memory growth over time
